lessonTitle: Archimedes and the area under a parabola
lessonTitleEnglish: Archimedes and the area under a parabola

stages.headline: Welcome! 2000 years before integrals, Archimedes found the area under y = x² from 0 to 1: it is 1/3.
stages.headlineEnglish: Welcome! 2000 years before integrals, Archimedes found the area under y = x² from 0 to 1: it is 1/3.

stages.headline: Today we do it in one line: x³/3 is an antiderivative of x², so the integral from 0 to 1 is 1/3 − 0 = 1/3.
stages.headlineEnglish: Today we do it in one line: x³/3 is an antiderivative of x², so the integral from 0 to 1 is 1/3 − 0 = 1/3.

optionsQuiz.feedbackIncorrect: 🤔 Not quite. The correct answer is {correctText}.

stages.headline: Compute /K \int_0^3 x^2\,dx K/.
stages.problemText: Compute the integral of x^2 from 0 to 3.
stages.solutionSteps: 1. x³/3 is an antiderivative of x². 2. 27/3 − 0 = 9.
